A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same factorial referential-communication study and corpus. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including content relocated in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original results from 89 pairs producing 356 dialogues, participant surveys, follow-up AI–AI experiments and extraction-validation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original communication experiment, participant-survey outcomes, follow-up experiments and validation results.

M1.justification: The GPT-5.2 setup, director/matcher prompts, JSON scaffolding and extraction procedure remain unchanged. Added descriptions of dialogue history and updated matcher images clarify the existing setup rather than establish new components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English basket-matching task, four pairing conditions and four rounds. The validation corpus of 800 expressions from 80 transcripts is retained and newly identified, not added.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same human/AI conditions and GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro and Claude Opus-4.5 pairings. Tables 2, 7 and 8 retain identical comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the Human–AI and AI–Human pair counts from 17 and 22 to 22 and 17, matching Tables 4–5 in both versions. This corrects reported sample allocation; it does not establish new recruitment or reruns.

E4.justification: The prompt simplification, reasoning-effort and mixed-model follow-ups, metric correlations, extraction validation and dialogue examples are retained. Expanded explanations of ordering errors do not introduce a separate test or new case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% confidence intervals, OLS significance levels, survey and validation standard deviations, and up to two runs per follow-up condition. No uncertainty-reporting practice or repeated-run count changes.

E6.justification: All eight tables retain their numerical entries, and Figure 2 retains its plotted results. Section 5 corrects the attribution of the 12.58% perceived human-likeness result from Human–AI alone to the pooled mixed conditions, consistent with Table 5.

T1.justification: The relative lexical-overlap and Jaccard definitions remain unchanged. Clarifying content-word counts and stating the existing overlap measure's 0–1 range add explanation without new mathematical reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The factorial-study novelty claim, corpus contribution and central conclusions about AI partners' grounding failures remain. The rewritten abstract states the existing findings more explicitly without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive distinction between temporary conceptual pacts and community conventions, connecting it to LLM training. Section 5 explicitly identifies basket-order errors alongside lack of entrainment as explanations for declining accuracy; the principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a repository location and describes the corpus as publicly available, replacing future-release statements. It identifies the validation corpus and clarifies concealed partner identity, dialogue/image context and aggregation across pairs.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of Jones et al. (2026), cites Jefferson (1989) for conversational timing and identifies Lockridge and Brennan (2001) as the validation source. These are limited extensions to the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract, background, methods and results, corrects several cross-references and replaces draft-like AI–human commentary with more formal prose. The main section sequence and most of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redesigned from five small panels in one row into an enlarged three-plus-two arrangement with distinct condition markers. Appendix material is regrouped, Table 6 becomes column-width, and Figure 10's overlapping prompt text and broken box are repaired.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and reproducibility through corrected cohort counts and survey attribution, an identified validation source and concrete access information. The redesigned Figure 2 and repaired Figure 10 improve readability. These are useful but limited gains; the experimental evidence and broad conclusions remain essentially unchanged.
